title.description: Large heading with an optional one-paragraph subtitle. For opening and closing cards.

statement.description: Heading with one or two short paragraphs making a single argument.

bullets.description: Heading, two to six bullets, and an optional closing paragraph.

comparison.description: Heading and two or three columns, each with a short heading and two to five items.

process.description: Heading and three to six ordered steps, each with a title and optional detail.

quote.description: A single quotation with attribution and an optional heading.

stats.description: Heading, two to four headline figures with labels, and an optional paragraph.

image-left.description: Photo on the left half; heading with a short paragraph or two to four bullets on the right.

image-right.description: Heading with a short paragraph or two to four bullets on the left; photo on the right half.

cover.description: Full-bleed photo behind a large heading and optional subtitle. For openings, section breaks, and closings.

chart.description: Heading and one chart of real figures, with an optional short paragraph, two to four bullets, or a callout reading the chart. The chart's size sets its share of the width beside the text; a full chart sits above the text.

table.description: Heading and one table of two to five columns and up to eight rows, with an optional paragraph or callout. The table's size sets its share of the width beside the text; a full table sits above it.

dashboard.description: Heading and two to four widgets (charts, progress meters, tables, callouts) in up to two rows. Widgets fill a row left to right by size: small is a third, medium a half, large two thirds, full the whole row.

card.position: number, as assigned in the plan
card.layout: one of title, statement, bullets, comparison, process, quote, stats, image-left, image-right, cover, chart, table, dashboard
card.nodes: array of nodes in reading order
card.sourceIds: array of research source IDs the card uses, e.g. s1

image.note: Never write image nodes. For a layout that holds an image, the image node is added for you; draft only the text nodes.

chart.kind: one of column, bar, stacked-column, line, area, pie, donut
chart.size: one of small, medium, large, full

series.name: string
values: number, one per category, without units

chart.prefix: optional string written before values, e.g. $
chart.suffix: optional string written after values, e.g. % or B
chart.caption: optional string naming where the figures come from

progress.size: one of small, medium, large, full

table.size: one of small, medium, large, full

callout.size: one of small, medium, large, full

widgets.data: Charts, meters, and tables show only figures stated in the research sources or the user's notes. Never invent, estimate, or round figures into new ones; when the figures are missing, use a text layout instead.

kinds.column: values compared across a few categories, or a short series over time
kinds.bar: values compared across categories with long names, or ranked
kinds.stacked-column: how two to four parts make up each category's total
kinds.line: change over time across many periods, for one to four series
kinds.area: change in one or two totals over time, where the volume matters
kinds.pie: parts of one whole, two to six slices; one series only
kinds.donut: parts of one whole with the total as the point; one series only

widgets.sizes: small is a third of a row, medium a half, large two thirds, full the whole row. In a chart or table card the size is the widget's share of the width beside the text, and a full widget sits above it.
widgets.tones: note for context, positive for a gain or success, caution for a risk or limit
